title: What If the Moon Was Twice as Close?
alt_titles: What If the Moon Were Half as Far Away? The Real Math
Moon at Half the Distance: 8× Tides and Total Eclipses Only
description:
Halve the Moon's distance and it looks twice as wide. Every tide on Earth gets 8 times stronger.

We run the scenario through real physics with every calculation on screen: the new sky, a 9.9-day lunar month, eclipses that are always total, equilibrium tides, the Roche limit, tidal braking and whether you'd feel it.

0:00 Intro
0:13 Moving the Moon
1:17 A bigger, faster Moon
2:37 Eclipses, upgraded
3:19 Eight times the tide
4:29 What happens at the coast
5:38 Would the Moon survive?
6:02 Longer days, faster
7:06 Would you feel it?
7:38 What we learned

🧮 The numbers (computed in code, rounded)
• Energy to move the Moon in: 3.8 × 10²⁸ J ≈ 100 s of the Sun's total output
• Apparent size: 0.53° → 1.07°, about 4× the light
• Orbit: 9.7 days, full Moon every 9.9 days
• Tidal force × 8; equilibrium tide range 54 cm → 4.3 m
• Roche limit ≈ 18,000 km, new orbit 10× farther out
• Day lengthening 2.3 → 150 ms per century

How this video was made: animations are generated from code; the narration voice is synthetic (text-to-speech); every number is computed by our calculation script and checked against the sources above.
